transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

Yes, a few ideas. Food freezing at the back of the fridge is common, and it's often something simple rather than a broken part. In rough order of likelihood: 1. The setting is too cold, or fast-freeze or super-cool has been left on. Check the fridge dial or display: about 3–5°C is right. On a numbered dial, the higher number is usually colder. If fast-freeze or super-cool is lit, switch it off. If it was on its coldest setting or a boost mode was on, that is very likely your answer. 2. Food is touching the back wall or sitting in front of a vent. The back wall of a fridge gets very cold, and many Hotpoint fridge-freezers also blow cold air in from the freezer through a vent near the back. Lettuce and yoghurts pushed up against either can freeze even when the rest of the fridge is at the right temperature. Move things an inch or two forward and don't pack the back tightly. If only the items at the very back freeze and the front is fine, this points strongly to airflow or placement. 3. A control fault, which is less likely. If the setting is normal and the food is clear of the back, a thermostat or temperature sensor reading wrong, or an air flap (damper) stuck open, can over-chill the fridge. It's worth putting a cheap fridge thermometer in a glass of water on the middle shelf. If it reads well below 3°C after a day on a normal setting, that suggests a control fault rather than placement. After changing anything, give it about 24 hours with the doors shut to settle before judging. To start, what is the dial or display set to at the moment, and is a fast-freeze or super-cool light on?
dial is turned right up to max/coldest, kids may have moved it. no lights, its just a knob inside

That's very likely your answer. With the dial on maximum the fridge runs as cold as it can, and the back wall gets coldest of all, so lettuce and yoghurts there will freeze solid. Small fingers turning the knob is a very common cause. Here's what I'd do: 1. Turn the knob back to a middle setting, around 3 on a 1–5 dial. On most Hotpoint knobs a higher number means colder. If you go too low the fridge can get warm, so start in the middle.
2. Keep food an inch or two away from the back wall and any vent. That way, even at the right setting, nothing is pressed against the coldest surface.
3. Leave it about 24 hours with the doors shut so it can settle. If you have a fridge thermometer, stand it in a glass of water on the middle shelf. Somewhere between 3 and 5°C is right.
4. Keep an eye on the freezer too. On some fridge-freezers one knob controls both sections, so turning it down slightly may warm the freezer a little. It should still keep food frozen hard. If food is still freezing after a day on a middle setting with it clear of the back, the setting wasn't the whole story. Then a faulty thermostat, or an air flap stuck open letting freezer air in, becomes the likely cause, and we can look at that next. Once it's settled, is anything still freezing, or is it back to normal?
ok turned it to the middle and cleared the vents, its better after 2 days but one yoghurt still froze right at the very back. is that normal?

Mostly, yes. If it's just one item right at the very back, that's quite common and usually not a fault. The back wall is the coldest surface in the fridge. On many models the cooling plate sits behind it, and frost or ice can form on it as part of normal running. Anything touching it, or sitting right where the cold air comes in, can freeze even when the rest of the fridge is at the right temperature. The big improvement since you turned the dial down points to the setting being the main problem, and that's now sorted. A few simple things will settle it:
1. Keep a gap of an inch or two between food and the back wall. Watery things like yoghurt, lettuce and soft fruit freeze most easily, so keep them near the front or in the salad drawer. If nothing freezes once there's a gap, it's just placement and normal.
2. If food still freezes with a clear gap, turn the dial down one notch and give it another 24 hours. Fridges vary, and the middle setting can be a little cold in a cool room. Check the freezer still keeps food frozen hard.
3. If you have a fridge thermometer, stand it in a glass of water on the middle shelf. Anywhere from 3 to 5°C is right. If it's around there, the odd item freezing at the very back is down to position, not a fault. If food keeps freezing well away from the back wall, or the middle shelf reads close to 0°C even on a lower setting, that's no longer normal. Then the likely culprits are the thermostat reading wrong or an air flap stuck open letting freezer air through, and that would be worth an engineer's look. Was that yoghurt actually touching the back wall or sitting by the vent? And if you've got a thermometer in there, what does it read?
yes it was right against the back wall i think. no thermometer, dont have one. should i just leave it then?

Yes, I'd mostly leave it. A yoghurt pressed right against the back wall freezing is normal: that wall is the coldest surface in the fridge, and anything touching it can freeze even when the rest is at the right temperature. The big improvement after turning the dial down shows the setting was the real problem, and that's now fixed. What I'd do from here:
1. Leave a gap of an inch or two between food and the back wall. Keep watery things like yoghurt, lettuce and soft fruit towards the front or in the salad drawer. If nothing freezes with a gap, it's just placement and nothing is wrong.
2. If something still freezes even with a clear gap, turn the dial down one notch and give it another day. Check the freezer still keeps food frozen hard.
3. Optional: a fridge thermometer only costs a few pounds and takes the guesswork out. In a glass of water on the middle shelf, 3–5°C is right. When it would stop being normal: food freezing on the front of the shelves or in the door, or still freezing well away from the back wall on a lower setting. That points to the thermostat reading wrong or an air flap stuck open letting freezer air through, and an engineer's look would be worth it then. Until then, it sounds like it's behaving as it should.
